Home / Introduction

Introduction to Operations Manager

Operations Manager (OM) is Cedar Gate's central platform for coordinating client data processing operations. It connects account setup, file delivery, processing execution, quality review, and production release into one trackable workflow.

  • Production URL: https://om.cgt.us/
  • Primary users: CPMs, Processing engineers, USDMs, Client Success, and Admin staff
  • Documentation source: Confluence OM space + OM application repositories (frontv2, api, filemanager, processing services)

OM replaces manual spreadsheets and email chains with structured processing tickets, automated calendar-driven scheduling, file inventory tracking, and integrated reporting.

Tip Bookmark the Dashboard — it is your default landing page after login.

Purpose & Business Overview

OM supports the end-to-end lifecycle of healthcare analytics data processing for Cedar Gate clients:

  1. Client setup — Accounts, applications, products, and team assignments
  2. File intake — S3 jobs deliver vendor files; File Inventory tracks receipt and staging
  3. Processing execution — Tickets progress through defined phases with cluster/job automation
  4. Quality & compliance — Daily IQR, SQR variance, JetStore test harness, SLA tracking
  5. Release & reporting — Production Release notifications, billing reports, audit trails

End-to-end operational flow

Accounts (master data)
    ├── Production Manager (tickets & phases)
    │       └── Jobs / Processing Dashboard (execution)
    ├── File Manager (inventory & missing files)
    ├── Reports / SLA Reports (metrics & compliance)
    └── Integrations (Jira, Salesforce, JetStore)

Key Features & Modules

Accounts

Client master data — accounts, applications, products, frequencies, and team assignments. Active/Termed tabs, Add Account, and role columns (CSL, USDM, CPM).

Home Dashboard

Landing view with previous/current month release trackers, maintenance status table, and cross-ticket Search.

Production Manager

Assignments board (US Team / Nepal Team) and Processing Tickets. Click a person or team tag to open Daily, Pending, Running, PAE, and Recent work queues.

Phase Tracker

Per-ticket hub: versions, File Received Date, flags (Autopilot, Special Processing), Effort Log, Update phase, and History audit trail. Includes File Arrangement, Scrub Request, and Autopilot workflows.

File Manager

File Inventory tabs for Staged Implementation/Production, Unstaged, and Missed files. Filter by Account, Application, and Product.

Jobs

Manage Jobs (per account/application) and Job Status. Find S3 Job and Search Files shortcuts for Processing and Admin roles.

Reports

Operational and billing report picker (SQR, Bad Data, Billing, Daily IQR Summary, CM/HP Test Results, and more) with Show and export.

SLA Reports

Client SLA Report and Configuration. Filter by account, application, and date range; export PDF/Excel.

Admin

Team Setup, SLA Setup, Daily IQR Setup, Version Management, Product Management, and Server Management (Admin only).

Processing Dashboard

Processing Cluster and Snowflake Cluster views. Monitor Client Processing, Daily IQR, Splitter, Parser, CA Fetch, and step-level status.

Module: Account Workflow Deep Dive

Overview and Purpose

Accounts is the master-data foundation of OM. Every processing ticket, job, file inventory record, and report is scoped to an Account → Application → Product.

  • What it does: Create and maintain client organizations (Accounts), their Applications, product–frequency combinations, team assignments, and operational flags (Onshore, Blinded Client, Implementation, Autopilot, DPCC#).
  • Business value: Single source of truth for who the client is, which products they buy, who owns the work (USDM, CPM, AM/Client Success Lead), and how processing should behave.
  • Fits into the system: Upstream of Production Manager, Jobs, File Manager, Reports, and SLA. Downstream of Salesforce sync for market segment and some contact fields.
Core Components
  • Active / Termed tabs — live vs terminated accounts/applications
  • Add/Edit Account panel — Account Code, Name, Acronym, Team Type, products, Implementation, Onshore, EDM, Name in Salesforce
  • Application panel — Application Code/Name/Acronym, Prod/UAT Billable Dates, Client App, Onshore Type, BOB, PCL, 3M, PGIC, Sandbox, Blinded Client, Processing Engine
  • Processing–Frequency — Product + Frequency + Autopilot + DPCC# + Skip Crosswalk Validation + Weekend Processing
  • Application Hierarchy — parent/child multi-scrub relationships
  • Show/Hide Fields — per-user column preferences
  • Generate PIN / Termination checklist / Notifications — lifecycle actions

Key terminology

TermMeaning
AccountTop-level client (e.g. 90 Degree Benefits)
ApplicationSub-entity under an Account (e.g. CAP, ALD)
Product–FrequencyDeliverable + cadence (PA–Monthly, CM–Daily)
Implementation flagYes = UAT/onboarding; No = Production
Blinded ClientYes / File Set / No — drives PHI de-identification
DPCC#Open change-control ticket that can hold processing

Dependencies

  • Salesforce (OMSF) — market segment, team, contacts, Implementation sync
  • Admin → Team Setup — Development Team options and Data Team User
  • Admin → Deerwalk Default SLA — Client SLA Days when adding products in Production
  • User Management — AUAT/CUAT/Production URLs
Detailed Workflow

Workflow

1. Admin/CPM opens Accounts → Add Account
2. Enter Account + first Application (auto-mirrors Account name/acronym)
3. Select Products → default Monthly frequency applied
4. If Implementation=No → set Client SLA Days per product
5. Assign CSL, USDM/CPM via Team; set Onshore / Blinded Client flags
6. Configure Processing–Frequency (Autopilot, DPCC#, Weekend Processing)
7. Optional: Application Hierarchy, S3 Encryption Key, Client Configuration
8. Save → SF sync; Deermine client list updated

Decision points & exceptions

  • Terming an Application → all open processing tickets auto-close
  • Adding a new product in Production → popup requires non-zero Client SLA Days
  • 3M flag editable only when Contract Analytics product is selected
  • Onshore Type required only when Onshore = Yes
  • Terminate Account enabled only when checklist items are Completed or N/A
Use Cases and Scenarios

Beginner

  1. Open Accounts → Active. Expand a row to see Applications and Products.
  2. Click Account Name to view read-only account details; download Excel if needed.
  3. Use Show/Hide Fields (gear) to display CSL and USDM columns.

Real-world

  1. New client signed: Admin creates Account + Application, sets Implementation=Yes, assigns products PA/CM, generates PIN, adds notification emails.
  2. Client goes live: flip Implementation to No, set Prod Billable Date, confirm SLA Days.
  3. Special processing month: set DPCC# and Autopilot=No on Product–Frequency.

Advanced

  1. Multi-scrub: define Application Hierarchy; child tickets inherit Special Processing from parent.
  2. Blinded Client = File Set: coordinate with Blinding Status / JetStore pseudonymization jobs.
  3. Weekend Processing=Yes: calendar events on Sat/Sun create tickets same day (OM-5564).
Configuration and Setup
  • Prerequisites: Admin or CPM role; Team exists in Admin → Team Setup; products registered in Product Management
  • Options: Team Type (Channel Partner / Direct Contract), Processing Engine (EMR / FME Only in Snowflake), Sandbox App, PGIC, Autopilot Processing
  • Best practices: Keep Acronym unique and aligned with SF; always set Name in Salesforce when acronym missing; verify Billable Dates before billing month-end

How it works — Data model & privileges How it works

Accounts is the configuration root. Roles: Admin can Add/Edit Account; CPM can edit Application-level info and assign products on existing accounts.

Field / actionBehavior
Account CodeAuto-increment 4-digit unique integer (read-only)
Account Name / AcronymUnique; acronym 3 chars — used in ticket naming and S3 ClientName
Market / Sub-Market SegmentView-only in OM; synced from Salesforce
Team TypeChannel Partner or Direct Contract — drives Team Setup routing
Implementation = YesUAT path; product add does not require Client SLA Days popup
Implementation = NoProduction; adding a product requires non-zero Client SLA Days (seeded from Admin Default SLA) and updates SLA Configuration
Term ApplicationAuto-closes all open processing tickets for that application
Billable datesIf Implementation=No, at least one active application must have a billable date
Generate PINCreates PIN, can upload to Drive and post Deermine tickets
Quarterly password emailPrimary application only; BCC om@cedargate.com on client key emails
How it works — Processing–Frequency engine How it works

Each Product–Frequency row is the switchboard for ticket create and Autopilot:

  • Autopilot Processing Yes/No (default No) — calendar/manual tickets assign to Autopilot User when Yes and unblocked.
  • DPCC# — open/valid DPCC holds create and Autopilot kickoff to Production CPM.
  • Weekend Processing — if enabled, calendar events on Sat/Sun create same day; else roll to Monday.
  • Skip Crosswalk Validation — influences Scrub Request validation path.
  • Client SLA Days — product-wise target used by SLA Reports and Outside target math.
Accounts Product–Frequency
    ├──► Production Manager ticket create (assignee/phase)
    ├──► Autopilot cron eligibility
    ├──► Phase Tracker summary flags (Autopilot, DPCC#)
    └──► SLA Reports Configuration (Client SLA Days)
How it works — Hierarchy & multi-scrub How it works
  1. Parent/child Application Hierarchy links multi-scrub clients.
  2. Calendar still has child events, but automation creates tickets only for events present — do not auto-create orphan children.
  3. Children scrub to Scrub Release; parent Application Processing Request waits for all children.
  4. Parent FRD at Application Processing Request = max FRD among children.
  5. Closing parent can close non-daily children still in Scrub Release.
Summary and Key Takeaways
  • Accounts is the dependency root — wrong flags cascade into tickets, files, and SLA
  • Success factor: keep Product–Frequency and Autopilot/DPCC accurate before month start
  • Next steps: configure Team Setup → create Account → set Processing–Frequency → verify Dashboard Search finds the client
Overview

Account Workflow is the master-data foundation of Operations Manager (OM). Every processing ticket, job, file inventory record, SLA measurement, and report is scoped to Account → Application → Product–Frequency.

Administrators and CPMs create and maintain client organizations, applications, product cadences, operational flags (Onshore, Blinded Client, Implementation, Autopilot, DPCC#), team ownership, PIN generation, and termination checklists.

Salesforce (OMSF) synchronizes market segment, team, contacts, and selected Implementation fields so OM stays aligned with commercial systems of record.

Related modules: Production Manager · Phase Tracker · SLA Reports · Set Up Documentation · Jira Automation

Business Purpose

Provide a single source of truth for who the client is, which products they buy, who owns the work, and how processing should behave under Autopilot, DPCC holds, weekend processing, and blinding rules.

Prevent cascading defects in Production Manager, Phase Tracker, Client SLA Days, File Inventory pathing, and billing custom reports.

  • Operational control: Autopilot, DPCC#, Weekend Processing, Skip Crosswalk Validation
  • Commercial alignment: Billable dates, Implementation vs Production, Salesforce name/acronym
  • Compliance posture: Blinded Client, Onshore / Onshore Type, PIN and termination audit trail
Key Features
  • Active and Termed tabs
  • Add/Edit Account: Code, Name, Acronym, Team Type, products, Implementation, Onshore, EDM, Name in Salesforce
  • Application panel: billable dates, Client App, Onshore Type, BOB, PCL, 3M, PGIC, Sandbox, Blinded Client, Processing Engine
  • Processing–Frequency: Product + Frequency + Autopilot + DPCC# + Skip Crosswalk + Weekend Processing + Client SLA Days
  • Application Hierarchy for multi-scrub parent/child
  • Show/Hide Fields, Generate PIN, Termination checklist, notification contacts
  • Salesforce sync for market segment, team, contacts, Implementation

Navigation Path
  1. Sign in to OM (QC / UAT / Production).
  2. Open Accounts (Account Management).
  3. Select Active or Termed.
  4. Expand a row for Applications and Product–Frequency.
  5. Use Add/Edit, Generate PIN, Termination, or Notifications as authorized.
Prerequisites
  • Admin or CPM for create/edit (or view rights)
  • Team exists in Team Setup with Data Team User when needed
  • Products registered; Deerwalk Default SLA configured for Production adds
  • Salesforce acronym / Name in Salesforce when OMSF sync required
  • PHI access governed by Blinded Client and Onshore policies
Configuration Steps
  1. Accounts → Add Account (or edit Active row).
  2. Enter Account + first Application; select Team Type and Development Team.
  3. Assign products (default Monthly frequency).
  4. If Implementation = No, enter Client SLA Days > 0 per product.
  5. Set Processing–Frequency flags: Autopilot, DPCC#, Weekend Processing, Skip Crosswalk.
  6. Set Onshore/Onshore Type, Blinded Client, 3M (with CA), PGIC, Sandbox, Processing Engine.
  7. Optional: Hierarchy, S3 Encryption Key, notifications.
  8. Save; confirm Salesforce sync.
Workflow Process

Account lifecycle

Workflow

1. Create Account + Application (Implementation usually Yes for onboarding)
2. Assign products/frequencies; set team ownership (USDM, CPM, CSL)
3. Generate PIN; add CMA/notification contacts for Autopilot authorization
4. Flip Implementation to No; set Prod Billable Date; confirm Client SLA Days
5. Maintain DPCC#, Autopilot, Weekend Processing before cycle start
6. Termination checklist → Terminate → open tickets auto-close

Terming an Application auto-closes open processing tickets. Client SLA Days > 0 required when adding products in Production. 3M editable only with Contract Analytics. Onshore Type required when Onshore = Yes.

Processing Logic

Account flags copy onto tickets and Phase Tracker (Onshore, VBCA, PGIC, 3M, Autopilot, DPCC#).

Production Manager create inspects open DPCC and running tickets for On Hold → Production CPM.

Hierarchy sequences child scrub before parent App Processing; FRD may use max-of-children.

Blinded Client = File Set coordinates with JetStore pseudonymization jobs.

FAQ

Q: What is Product–Frequency?
A: Product + cadence + operational flags (Autopilot, DPCC#, etc.).

Q: Who terminates accounts?
A: Admin/CPM after checklist Completed/N/A.

Q: Where does Autopilot live?
A: On Product–Frequency; honored by Production Manager and Phase Tracker.

Operational Impact

Misconfigured accounts cause wrong Autopilot assignment, bad SLA clocks, SF sync failures, and inventory path errors. Treat account changes as change-controlled master data.

Dependencies
  • Team Setup and Deerwalk Default SLA
  • Product Management / Product Roles and Rights
  • Salesforce OMSF
  • Production Manager, Phase Tracker, File Inventory, SLA Reports
Audit and Compliance Considerations

Account edits, PIN generation, and terminations are auditable. Blinded Client and Onshore are PHI controls; billable dates and SLA days are FI-sensitive.

  • Retain termination checklist evidence
  • Avoid PHI in notification free text
  • Align Salesforce and OM identifiers before audits
Examples and Scenarios

Scenario A: New PA monthly client — Implementation=Yes → PA/PAE → PIN → go-live Implementation=No, SLA Days=5, Autopilot=Yes.

Scenario B: DPCC hold — CPM sets DPCC#; create places ticket On Hold → Production CPM.

Scenario C: Multi-scrub hierarchy — children scrub before parent App Processing.

Administrative Guidance

Administrative actions

  1. Maintain Team Setup and Product Roles before mass creates
  2. Enforce unique acronyms and Salesforce mapping
  3. Review Implementation flags during go-live waves
  4. Gate Terminate on checklist; verify auto-close
  5. Coordinate Blinded Client with Security/JetStore
End-User Guidance

End-user actions

  1. Work from Active, not Termed
  2. Verify Autopilot/DPCC# before escalating missing tickets
  3. Ask CPM/Admin for master-data changes
  4. Prefer Account/Application codes in search
Known Limitations and Constraints
  • 3M requires Contract Analytics product
  • Some SF fields are sync-owned
  • Termination auto-close may miss rare manual tickets
  • Large Active lists need pagination

Module: Contract Analytics (CA) Processing Deep Dive

Overview

Contract Analytics (CA) Processing exposes CA workload health in OM while DevOps manages the shared EMR cluster lifecycle.

The CA Fetch tab shows date-ranged jobs, timing, state, and log links without providing a cluster-terminate control.

Related modules: Jobs · Dashboard · Version Management · Account Workflow

Business Purpose

Give CA and Operations a governed operational view of queued analytic jobs.

Protect shared infrastructure: OM can monitor and request launch metadata, while DevOps alone can manually terminate clusters.

  • Give CA and Operations a governed operational view of queued analytic jobs.
  • CA Fetch Processing tab
  • Apply role-based access and protect PHI/FI.
Key Features
  • CA Fetch Processing tab
  • Date From / Date To job search
  • DevOps-managed cluster launch API
  • Job queue monitoring
  • syslog, stderr, and stdout links
  • Failure mail to caexceptionmailgroup
  • One-hour idle auto-termination
User Roles and Permissions
Role / PersonaCapabilities
DevOpsLaunches and manually terminates CA clusters
CA TeamSubmits jobs and reviews logs
OM AdminMaintains queue and notification configuration
Processing/CPMCoordinates status; cannot terminate clusters

Capabilities are role-scoped; do not expose PHI or financial information beyond business need.

Navigation Path
  1. Sign in to OM.
  2. Open Processing Dashboard.
  3. Select CA Fetch Processing.
  4. Set Date From and Date To, then inspect results.
Prerequisites
  • CA Client UI submits jobs to the queue
  • DevOps CA/EMR cluster is available
  • caexceptionmailgroup is configured
  • User can view the CA Fetch tab
Configuration Steps
  1. Validate environment API endpoints.
  2. Keep the queue consumer active.
  3. Set idle policy to one hour.
  4. Ensure no OM terminate button is exposed.
  5. Test failure mail routing.
Workflow Process

CA Processing workflow

Workflow

1. CA Client UI submits work to the OM job queue
2. OM dispatches queued work to the DevOps CA cluster
3. CA Fetch searches jobs using Date From and Date To
4. Operators inspect syslog, stderr, or stdout for failures
5. Idle cluster terminates after one hour; DevOps owns manual termination
Field Definitions
FieldContextMeaning
Date From / ToFilterRequired start-date range; normally yesterday through today
Job NameResultCA workload identifier
Start / EndResultExecution timestamps
Total TimeResultCalculated duration
StatusResultQueued, Running, Completed, or Failed
LogsResultLinks to syslog, stderr, and stdout
Screens and Components
  • CA Fetch filter
  • Job results grid
  • Status/timing columns
  • Log links
  • Processing Dashboard context
Status Definitions
StatusDefinition
QueuedWaiting for CA capacity
RunningExecuting on EMR
CompletedFinished successfully
FailedFailure mail is sent
Cluster IdleNo work; one-hour termination countdown
Processing Logic

Jobs are queue-driven, not bound to one processing ticket.

Date filters restrict the operational view; Date To cannot precede Date From.

A failed job is actionable through its logs and exception mail.

OM intentionally has no CA cluster terminate action.

Validation Rules
  • Require both dates.
  • Reject inverted date ranges.
  • Prevent duplicate uncontrolled retries.
  • Restrict log access to authorized users.
Automation and Integrations
  • Queue dispatch to CA EMR
  • One-hour idle auto-termination
  • Failure notification to caexceptionmailgroup
  • DevOps launch-information API

Related modules: Jobs · Dashboard · Version Management · Account Workflow

Reporting Capabilities

CA Fetch is the operational report; narrow date filters before exporting the visible grid.

Notifications and Alerts
  • Failed-job mail to caexceptionmailgroup
  • DevOps paging remains outside OM
  • Notifications reference job IDs, not PHI
Best Practices
  • Review Failed rows daily
  • Use short date windows
  • Escalate infrastructure to DevOps
  • Keep raw logs out of email
Common Use Cases

Beginner

  1. Open CA Fetch for today
  2. Filter Failed and open stderr

Real-world

  1. Review overnight CA batch
  2. Use exception mail to assign remediation

Advanced

  1. Correlate a CA failure to related PA version context
  2. DevOps checks launch metadata
Troubleshooting Guide
SymptomLikely causeResolution
No jobsDate range excludes work or queue is stalledWiden dates and ask DevOps to check queue
Cannot terminateBy designContact DevOps
No mailDistribution list issueValidate caexceptionmailgroup
Repeated attemptsRetry policy issueReview queue controls
FAQ

Q: Can OM terminate CA?
A: No; DevOps can, and idle clusters auto-terminate after one hour.

Q: Who receives failure mail?
A: caexceptionmailgroup.

Q: Where are logs?
A: The job row links to syslog, stderr, and stdout.

Operational Impact

CA disruption delays analytic deliverables but should not disrupt normal PA/CM processing.

Unauthorized termination could interrupt shared work.

Dependencies
  • DevOps EMR cluster
  • CA Client UI / queue
  • Jobs
  • Version Management
  • Mail relay
Audit and Compliance Considerations

Retain job status and log-access evidence for incident review.

Use job identifiers in correspondence; logs may be sensitive.

  • Record configuration and status changes.
  • Limit PHI/FI exports and retain evidence under policy.
Examples and Scenarios

Overnight batch: two Failed jobs create exception mail and CA reviews stderr.

Idle control: the cluster stops one hour after the final job.

Administrative Guidance

Administrative actions

  1. Review queue depth
  2. Maintain exception group
  3. Verify terminate remains absent
  4. Coordinate API changes with DevOps
End-User Guidance

End-user actions

  1. Filter by a narrow date range
  2. Inspect logs before escalating
  3. Do not attach raw outputs to open channels
Known Limitations and Constraints
  • No OM-side manual termination
  • Cluster lifecycle is DevOps-owned
  • Large date ranges can return many logs

Processing Logic

Bad File Format can group by daily_iqr_id; Bad Data groups by client, data type, layout, and vendor.

Module: Dashboard Deep Dive

Overview and Purpose

The Home Dashboard is the post-login landing page for operational oversight of maintenance processing.

  • What it does: Shows Previous/Current month Completed–Missed–To be Completed counts by frequency and lists live maintenance tickets with Days Remaining colour coding.
  • Business value: Morning standup view — who is at risk, what was missed last month, what remains this month.
  • Fits into the system: Read-model over Production Manager tickets; Search spans archived tickets too.
Core Components
  • Previous Month Release Tracker (Completed / Missed)
  • Current Month Release Tracker (Completed / Missed / To be Completed)
  • Frequency toggles: Quarterly | Monthly (default) | Biweekly | Weekly
  • Latest Status of Maintenance tickets (by frequency groups)
  • Search panel (Account, Application, Product, Type, Ticket, Created Date range)
  • Edit icon on rows (CPM/Admin) for dates/status/versions
  • Data Client Summary email at 5 PM NPT to Production CPMs

Exclusions from trackers

  • Archived tickets, termed clients, Daily frequency, child applications, test processing
  • Current month also excludes latest phase Closed / On Hold
Detailed Workflow

Workflow

Login → Dashboard loads Monthly trackers for prev/current month
Toggle frequency if reviewing Weekly/Biweekly book of work
Click Completed/Missed/To be Completed → drill-down list
Scan Days Remaining colours (Red=At Risk, Yellow=Waiting, Sky Blue=Released)
Use Search for a specific client or ticket (includes archive)
Optional: Edit dates → Comment for Change mandatory
Use Cases and Scenarios

Beginner

  1. Find your client's ticket in Monthly group; open Processing Ticket link.
  2. Note Days Remaining colour before escalating.

Real-world

  1. CPM morning: open Current Month Missed drill-down; chase File Received delays.
  2. Export Search results for weekly leadership pack.

Advanced

  1. Reconcile Missed Late File Received sheet (Updated Scheduled Date > Original).
  2. Account for Waiting on ClearHealth time deducted from release calculations.
Configuration and Setup
  • Driven by Internal SLA Refresh Days (Admin → SLA Setup) for Release Date math
  • No per-user dashboard config beyond role-gated Edit
  • Best practice: treat EST timestamps as source of truth for dates
Roles and Responsibilities
RoleAccess
All rolesView Dashboard and Search
CPM / AdminEdit ticket dates, status, versions from table
Production CPMsReceive Data Client Summary email
Common Issues and Troubleshooting
ProblemCauseResolution
Ticket missing from tableReleased (non-Daily), archived, child app, or testUse Search including archive
Counts look wrongWrong frequency toggle or Release Date nullToggle Monthly; check Original Scheduled Date fallback
Cannot editRole is USER/USDM without edit rightsAsk CPM/Admin
Performance and Optimization
  • Prefer frequency-scoped views over loading all Daily+Monthly at once when possible
  • Use Search date ranges instead of scrolling large tables
  • Drill-downs support Excel export — use for offline analysis
Module Interactions
  • Reads Maintenance tickets from Production Manager
  • Edit actions write Phase Tracker fields (Scheduled Date, Status, Comment)
  • Release Date logic ties to Admin Internal SLA Refresh Days
  • Search results open Phase Tracker pages
Deep Dive — Trackers Explained Deep Dive
TrackerShowsExclusions
Previous Month Completed/MissedLast cycle outcomesArchived, termed, Daily, child apps, test
Current Month Completed/Missed/To be CompletedIn-flight book of workSame + current Closed/On Hold
Frequency togglesQuarterly / Monthly / Biweekly / WeeklyDaily never in these trackers

Days Remaining: Red = At Risk, Yellow = Waiting, Sky Blue = Released. Math uses Internal SLA Refresh Days (weekdays from Scheduled Date).

Deep Dive — Morning Standup Guide Deep Dive
  1. Open Current Month Missed then To be Completed.
  2. Drill tickets with red Days Remaining into Phase Tracker.
  3. Search (includes archive) for client pulls; export Excel for leadership.
  4. Reconcile with Data Client Summary email (5 PM NPT).
Deep Dive — Edit from Dashboard Deep Dive
  • CPM/Admin Edit: dates/status/versions — Comment for Change mandatory on date edits.
  • Linked PA/PAE/SCE fields may sync — verify companions after edit.
How it works — Release tracker math How it works
  • Release Date on each ticket = Scheduled Date + Internal SLA Refresh Days (UAT vs Production days from Admin), counting weekdays only, including Scheduled Date.
  • Days Remaining = business days between today and Release Date (shown on Dashboard table and Search).
  • Completed — released in window; Missed — past Release Date without completion; To be Completed — still open and due.
  • Daily frequency, child applications, archived, termed, and test tickets are excluded from tracker cards.
  • Current month also excludes tickets currently Closed or On Hold from “to be completed” pressure.
How it works — Search results model How it works

Search returns active and archived tickets with: Client, Product, Ticket, USDM, CPM(s), Phase, Created Date, Production Release Date, Scheduled Date, Days Remaining, Comments. Excel export preserves columns.

Use Created Date range (EST) to bound archive noise. Edit from Dashboard still requires Comment for Change on date updates and may sync PA↔PAE/SCE companions.

Summary and Key Takeaways
  • Dashboard = health check; Phase Tracker = workbench
  • Success factor: act on Red/Yellow Days Remaining before SLA breach
  • Next: open a Missed drill-down, then walk that ticket in Phase Tracker

Module: File Inventory Deep Dive

Overview and Purpose

File Manager tracks vendor file intake: staged QC/production files, unstaging to tickets, missed files, and related FM tools.

  • What it does: List inventory from S3 Copy/Parse/Static jobs; Move to Production; Set Processing ID; Expected Date/Frequency; Missed reporting.
  • Business value: Prevents processing with incomplete feeds; drives missing-file Jira and daily Missing File Report emails.
  • Fits into the system: Fed by Jobs; consumed by Phase Tracker File Arrangement / Unstaging; informs SLA File Delivery reports.
Core Components
  • Tabs: Staged Implementation ($), Missed Implementation, Staged Production (_!), Missed Production, Unstaged, Missed while Arranging, Missed Files
  • Filters: Account, Application, Product
  • Actions: Move to Production, Set Processing ID, Set Expected Date/Frequency, Required flag, Grace Period
  • Related: Client FM, General FM, Vendor Schedule, FTP Accounts, File Linkage API

Destination path convention

dasscrubinput/[Onshore/Offshore (Optional)]/[ClientName]/[ProductAcronym]/[Incremental (Optional)]/[StageFolder]/[ClientFolder]/[VendorName]/[FileType]/[Layout (Optional)]/[DateFolder]/[FileName]

  • ClientName = AccountAcronym_ApplicationAcronym (uppercase)
  • ClientFolder = AccountAcronym or AccountAcronym_ApplicationAcronym (lowercase)
  • ProductAcronym = PA / CM / HP / CMP / CMA / FME / CC (case-insensitive)
  • StageFolder = Stage0 or preFileProcess (case-insensitive)
  • DateFolder = %{yyyyMMdd|0}% (date regex)
Detailed Workflow

Workflow

S3 Job places file in dasscrubinput with staging $ or _!
Inventory lists file in Staged Implementation or Production
Optional: Move to Production (keep or drop $ copy)
Unstage via Set Processing ID or Phase = File Unstaging
File appears in Unstaged linked to ticket
If Expected Date passes with no new file → Missed tabs + email/Jira
Use Cases and Scenarios

Beginner

  1. Filter Account/Application/Product → Search Staged Production Files.
  2. Compare Expected Date vs File Received Date.

Real-world

  1. Move QC ($) files to Production before first live scrub.
  2. Investigate Missed Production Files before advancing File Arrangement.

Advanced

  1. Onshore Move to Production also unstages blinded/crosswalk/sample companions.
  2. S3 Static jobs appear in Unstaged/Missed without requiring a processing ticket.
Configuration and Setup
  • Job Staging must be Production (_!) or QC ($), not None
  • Destination path must match OM inventory convention
  • Frequency/Tolerance Days drive next Expected Date
  • Best practice: mark Required vs Optional accurately for triage
Roles and Responsibilities
RoleAccess
AllRead File Manager
CPMLimited write: Expected Date, Frequency on staged; FTP Accounts

Staged Production (_!)Live stagingUnstage / Set Processing ID

Deep Dive — Stage → Unstage Guide Deep Dive
  1. Confirm S3 job completed and destination path follows OM convention.
  2. Filter Account/Application/Product → Staged Production (or Move to Prod from $).
  3. Set Required / Expected Date / Frequency / Grace Period.
  4. Unstage via Set Processing ID or Phase Tracker → File Unstaging.
  5. Onshore Move to Prod may unstage Blinded Files too.
Path dasscrubinput/.../ClientName/Product/.../Stage0|preFileProcess/.../_!yyyyMMdd/file
Deep Dive — Related FM Tools Deep Dive
  • Client FM / General FM, Vendor Schedule, FTP Accounts, File Linkage API.
  • S3 Static inserts inventory without destination move; archived Static excluded from FM listings.

Related: File Unstaging · Jobs · Waiting for Files

How it works — Listing criteria How it works

A file appears in Inventory only when:

  1. Placed in dasscrubinput by S3 Copy/Parse (or Static with EOF invocation rule), and
  2. Staging is Production (_!) or QC ($) — not None, and
  3. Destination path matches the OM convention (ClientName, Product, Stage0/preFileProcess, date folder, etc.).

Failures land in untracked_file_inventory. Destinations with is_destination_removed=1 never list. File Received Date comes from OM SQS; Expected Date from job frequency (+ tolerance days).

How it works — Expected Date, Required, Missed How it works
  • Frequency options include Daily (24h window), Weekly, Biweekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Semiannually, On Hold, N/A.
  • Tolerance days adjust next Expected Date calculation.
  • Required flag (editable from Inventory) drives Autopilot missing-file holds vs skip.
  • When Expected Date passes with no new file → Missed tabs + Missing File automation (Deermine) + 9:15 AM Missing File Report.
  • Missed Files tab can list missed production files for a selected Expected Date across clients (excluding already received).
  • Unstage/re-unstage stores missing-file records visible from Phase Tracker.
How it works — Move to Prod & blinding How it works
  • Move to Production promotes $ staged files to production staging (optionally keep QC copy).
  • For onshore clients, Move to Prod also unstages corresponding Blinded Files when present.
  • Parse/Split introduces parent job linkage so vendor filename lineage is retained.
Summary and Key Takeaways
  • Staging prefixes ($ / _!) are the operational language of file readiness
  • Success factor: clear Missed Production before scrub
  • Next: configure S3 Jobs correctly; practice Move to Production in QC

On success: inventory/update paths; on fail: email + Job Status actions

Deep Dive — Job Types Deep Dive
TypeTriggerOutcome
S3 Copy / ParseFile / scheduleInventory + staging $ or _!
S3 StaticFile matchInventory only (no destination)
UploadPhase (Extract Upload)Extract delivery; multi sub-job PAE
Inbound / Auth / CM Outbound / EnginePhase matchProduct pipelines

Deep Dive — Configure & Monitor Deep Dive
  1. Account → Application → Add/Edit job (source, destination, staging, Files Required?, emails).
  2. Optional: Blind Files, Authorization File, Linked Job ID, destination copy.
  3. Job Status → Failed → Resume / Restart / Skip / Rerun after fix.
Important Phase-triggered jobs fire only when Phase Tracker sets the matching phase. See Phase-triggered Jobs.
Deep Dive — PAE Multi Upload Deep Dive

One Upload Job can hold multiple enabled source→destination sub-jobs. Any failure → ticket On Hold; recover in Job Status. See PAE Autopilot and Extract Upload.

How it works — S3 pipeline How it works
Vendor/S3 source
  → S3 Copy / Parse / Static (invocation rule + staging)
  → dasscrubinput path
  → File Inventory ($ or _!)
  → Unstage / Phase Tracker
  → Scrub
  • Copy/Parse: source, destination, staging, refresh/append, Files Required?, Blind Files, Authorization File, Linked Job ID.
  • Static: inventory tracking without destination move; archived Static excluded from Client/General FM.
  • Splitter: mandatory Crosswalk Type Dev/Prod; SQS routed to Dev/Priority/Production queues.
  • Vendor field resolves Vendor Relationship / Data Supplier for IFR identification.
How it works — Phase-triggered Upload How it works
  • Upload Job = copy from source path to destination when ticket hits configured Phase (Job Run By = phase).
  • Typical phase: Extract Upload for PAE/FME.
  • Multi sub-job (PAE 1.1): sequential children; any fail → ticket On Hold; Resume/Restart/Skip per sub-job.
  • ROLE_OM_USER is read-only on Upload tab.
How it works — Job Status lifecycle How it works
  1. Engine posts Running → Completed/Failed to OM API.
  2. Failed: email recipients from Assign Job Email; actions Resume / Restart / Skip / Rerun.
  3. Trash/Delete S3 jobs can notify; restore archived jobs where supported.
  4. PagerDuty / monitoring hooks exist for critical job failures.
Summary and Key Takeaways
  • Correct job config prevents 80% of inventory and scrub issues
  • Success factor: Job Status Failed = zero overnight
  • Next: map each client’s critical S3 jobs; document owners

Troubleshooting Guide
SymptomLikely causeResolution
Job stuckRunner/capacity issueCheck status and DevOps
Restart unavailableRole or terminal policyRequest authorized operator
S3 copy failedPath/IAM issueValidate source/destination access
Parse failedInput shape issueReview validation and source file
FAQ

Q: What is a static job?
A: A configured task that does not require dynamic parsing.

Q: Resume vs restart?
A: Resume continues a recoverable run; restart starts a new attempt.

Q: Can a job start before phase?
A: Only if its definition is not phase-triggered.

Operational Impact

Job failures can delay phases, file availability, and production releases.

Dependencies
  • Phase
  • File Manager
  • Production
  • S3 storage
  • Job runtime
Audit and Compliance Considerations

Keep run history, input references, and recovery rationale.

Restrict sensitive uploaded file access.

  • Record configuration and status changes.
  • Limit PHI/FI exports and retain evidence under policy.
Examples and Scenarios

Parse: a validated upload triggers a phase job.

Recovery: operator resumes a transiently failed S3 copy.

Administrative Guidance

Administrative actions

  1. Maintain definitions
  2. Review retry policies
  3. Audit restart rights
  4. Monitor runner health
End-User Guidance

End-user actions

  1. Use Job Status first
  2. Do not restart blindly
  3. Attach only approved evidence
Known Limitations and Constraints
  • Recovery depends on job type
  • S3/IAM dependencies apply
  • Large uploads may take time

Module: Phase Tracker Deep Dive

Overview and Purpose

Phase Tracker is the workbench for a single processing ticket — status, versions, comments, effort, and phase-driven automation.

  • What it does: Display summary; Update phase/assignee/comment; Edit Processing; Effort Log; History; trigger release/PAE/JetStore side effects.
  • Business value: Auditable lifecycle from File Arrangement → Scrub → Application Processing → Production/Extract Release.
  • Fits into the system: Centre of Operations Manager — Jobs, File Inventory, JetStore, and Reports all react to phase changes here.
Core Components
  • Summary: Account, Application, Ticket ID, versions, Onshore, FRD, Autopilot, DPCC#, flags
  • Icons: Parent/Child tickets, Product Ticket (PA/PAE/SCE), Show Files, File Inventory
  • Update panel: Phase, Assigned To, Comment, attachments
  • Edit Processing: dates, status, versions, Scrub Only, CETL, Re-Unstage, Skip Validation
  • Effort Log and History (filterable audit trail)
  • Process Job / Initiate RTI (role-gated)
Detailed Workflow

Workflow

Open ticket → Review Summary (versions, FRD, DPCC, Autopilot)
Update → select Phase + Assignee + Comment → Save
Phase side effects:
  File Unstaging → inventory unstage
  Scrub Request → DPCC / bad format / crosswalk / blind checks
  Production Release → PAE extract path + email + Last Release Ticket
  On Hold (PA) → linked PAE On Hold
History records every change; author can edit latest comment
Use Cases and Scenarios

Beginner

  1. Add a progress comment via Update without changing phase.
  2. Open History and filter by Phase = Scrubbing.

Real-world

  1. File Arrangement complete → Scrub Request → monitor cluster via Processing Dashboard.
  2. Production Release on PA → confirm PAE moves to Extract Upload/Release.

Advanced

  1. Re-release with email suppress/re-send prompts.
  2. Manually set Last Release Ticket for Incremental/Bulk Incremental matching rules.
  3. JetStore failure → On Hold assigned to Data Team User from Team Setup.
Configuration and Setup
  • Phases/products from Admin → Product Management
  • Versions from Admin → Version Management
  • Client Configuration (File Mapper) drives PAE extractUploadToFtp / Redshift flags
  • Best practice: Comment for Change mandatory on any date edit
Roles and Responsibilities
RoleAccess
Admin / CPMEdit Processing; most phase updates
ProcessingStart processing; specialized phases (Inbound, Extract Upload, File Unstaging)
USDMFile Unstaging; phase updates; cannot edit FRD manually
USER / AM(Client Success Lead)Update phase when assigned; comment; effort log
Common Issues and Troubleshooting
ProblemCauseResolution
Phase option missingRole restrictionEscalate to Processing/Admin
PAE not advancingextractFormat MSSQL/Custom or missing upload jobCheck Client Configuration + Upload Job
Stuck On HoldJetStore / DPCC / extract failureRead latest History comment; fix root cause
FRD wrongWaiting for Files not cleared or manual edit neededAdmin/Processing update FRD
Performance and Optimization
  • Keep comments concise; attach logs instead of pasting large text
  • Use History filters rather than scrolling long tickets
  • Avoid duplicate Production Release without need (triggers confirmation noise)
Module Interactions
  • File Manager — unstaging and Show Files inventory
  • Jobs / Processing Dashboard — scrub/app clusters and phase-triggered jobs
  • JetStore — implementation test harness status → On Hold / Jira defects
  • Reports — SQR / release notes consume release events
  • Jira — DPCC links, File Issues, Feature Defects
How it works — Update & side effects How it works

Update panel (hidden until Update clicked) sets Phase, Assignee, Comment, attachments, cycle dates. Every save writes History.

  • File Unstaging → file-manager unstage API (submit blocked while in progress).
  • Scrub Request → DPCC, Bad File Format, crosswalk, blind, I-Check, halt scrub-to-app.
  • Production Release → PAE extract path, release email, Last Release Ticket, auto-assignee.
  • On Hold on PA → linked PAE On Hold → Production CPM.
  • Closed on parent → non-daily children in Scrub Release also Closed.
  • Leaving Waiting for Files refreshes File Received Date; parent App Processing Request sets FRD to max(children).

Tip Process flow diagram summarizes the happy path; On Hold branches apply for DPCC, JetStore, and extract failures.

File Arrangement Process

File Arrangement is typically the first active phase for non-autopilot maintenance tickets (assigned to Processing Team). It is managed from Phase Tracker.

What happens

  1. Processing team verifies expected vendor files have arrived (File Inventory, Vendor Schedule)
  2. S3 jobs copy/parse files into dasscrubinput with correct staging paths
  3. Files appear in File Inventory under Staged Implementation ($) or Staged Production (_!) tabs
  4. When ready, files are unstaged and linked to the processing ticket

DPCC scan at File Arrangement

OM checks for open DPCC tickets for the client-product-frequency. If found, processing may be held pending CPM confirmation.

Phase progression

After files are arranged and validated, phase advances to Scrub Request or Waiting depending on client workflow and autopilot settings.

Scrub Request Workflow

Scrub Request initiates data scrubbing on arranged files. Update the phase from Phase Tracker after pre-scrub checks pass.

Pre-scrub validations

  • DPCC scan — open change controls may block processing
  • Bad File Format validation
  • Crosswalk validation (unless Skip Validation flag set)
  • Blind Run validation for blinded clients
  • I-Check execution where configured

Flags affecting scrub

  • Scrub Only — PA implementation tickets; scrub without full app processing
  • Re-Processing / Special Processing — affects version and branch selection
  • File Mapping Only — CPM can enable on Implementation tickets in Scrub Request phase

After scrub completes

Phase moves to Scrubbing → Application Processing Request → Application Processing → Sign-off → Production Release.

Autopilot Functionality

Autopilot reduces manual intervention for eligible client-product-frequency combinations. Autopilot tickets still surface in Phase Tracker for monitoring and exception handling.

Configuration

Set Autopilot Processing = Yes at Accounts → Application → Processing-Frequency panel.

Ticket creation behavior

When Autopilot is enabled and no blocking conditions exist (DPCC, running ticket), new calendar tickets assign to Autopilot User in Waiting phase instead of File Arrangement.

Product-specific autopilot

  • HBA Autopilot — healthcare analytics batch processing automation
  • CM Autopilot — Care Manager processing automation
  • CMA Autopilot — Care Manager Analytics automation
  • PA Autopilot in Child Tickets — parent-child multi-scrub client handling

PAE extract autopilot

When PA ticket reaches Production Release, linked PAE ticket may auto-advance to Extract Upload → Extract Release based on client configuration (extractUploadToFtp, extractImportToRedshift).

Tip Autopilot does not bypass DPCC or running-ticket checks — those always take priority.

Module: Production Manager Deep Dive

Overview and Purpose

Production Manager is the operations hub for creating, assigning, and tracking processing tickets (Implementation and Maintenance).

  • What it does: Assignments board, Create Processing, ticket lists (Development vs Production), archive, and Search.
  • Business value: Schedules work from MS Calendar and manual creates; routes tickets to Autopilot, Processing Team, Daily Production, or Production CPM.
  • Fits into the system: Consumes Accounts Product–Frequency; drives Phase Tracker lifecycle; triggers Jobs and PAE/SCE companion tickets.
Core Components
  • Assignments — US Team / Nepal Team tags with counts; drill into Daily, Pending, Running, PAE, Recent
  • Processing Tickets — Development (I) vs Production (M) tabs
  • Create Processing — Account, Application, Product–Frequency, Category, Type
  • Calendar automation — MS Calendar events → Maintenance tickets
  • Auto-archive — M: 150 days after release/closed; I: 90 days idle

Ticket naming

  • Maintenance: Account_Application_Product_MM_YY_Frequency (e.g. WBI_WBI_PAE_08_26_M1)
  • Implementation: Account_Application_Product_I# (e.g. ACL_COM_PA_I1)
Detailed Workflow

Workflow

Calendar event / Manual Create
  ├─ Open DPCC? → Waiting/On Hold → Production CPM
  ├─ Running ticket (non-daily)? → On Hold → Production CPM
  ├─ Autopilot=Yes? → Waiting → Autopilot User
  └─ Else PA/CM/HP → File Arrangement (non-daily) or Waiting Daily Production
Companion tickets: PAE / SCE / HP / Cohort when frequency matches
User works ticket in Phase Tracker → Release → Auto-archive timer starts

Pending vs Running (Assignments)

  • Pending phases: Waiting, File Arrangement, Scrub Request, Scrub Import, Scrub Resume, Application Processing Request, Extract Generation
  • Running: all other open non-daily phases
  • Daily tab: all daily tickets regardless of phase
Use Cases and Scenarios

Beginner

  1. Open Assignments → click your name tag → review Pending tab.
  2. Open a Processing Ticket link to enter Phase Tracker.

Real-world

  1. Month start: verify Scheduled Production Processing email (9:15 AM NPT) vs calendar.
  2. Manual Incremental create: ensure Bulk Incremental exists or validation blocks create.

Advanced

  1. Special Processing + DPCC#: ticket created with flag reflected to PAE/SCE and children.
  2. Weekend Processing config: tickets create on weekend event dates.
Configuration and Setup
  • MS Calendar event format: Account Application_Deliverable_Frequency-Category
  • Product–Frequency Autopilot / DPCC# / Weekend Processing on Accounts
  • Internal SLA Refresh Days → Release Date from Scheduled Date (weekdays only)
  • Best practice: Category defaults to Regular; validate Incremental prerequisites

Cannot create IncrementalNo Bulk Incremental for same client/product/typeCreate Bulk Incremental first

  • Archive completed tickets promptly (or rely on auto-archive)

TabCriteria
DailyAll daily tickets for assignee (any phase)
PendingNon-daily in Waiting, File Arrangement, Scrub Request/Import/Resume, App Processing Request, Extract Generation
RunningOther open non-daily tickets
PAEAll PAE tickets for assignee (also listed elsewhere if matching)
RecentLast updated by user within N days

Buckets also group by recency: <24h, <48h, >48h.

Deep Dive — Create Processing Deep Dive
  1. Create Processing → Account, Application, Product–Frequency, Category, Type.
  2. Incremental requires existing Bulk Incremental for same Account/App/Product.
  3. Open DPCC or running ticket may force On Hold → Production CPM.
  4. Companions (PAE/SCE/HP/Cohort) created when frequency matches.
  5. Release Date = Scheduled Date + Internal Refresh Days (UAT vs Prod, weekdays).
Create (Calendar or Manual)
  ├─ Open DPCC? → On Hold → Production CPM
  ├─ Running ticket (non-daily)? → On Hold
  ├─ Autopilot=Yes? → Waiting → Autopilot User
  └─ Else → File Arrangement or Waiting (Daily Production)
Deep Dive — Archive & Search Deep Dive
  • Maintenance archive: 150 days after Release/Closed.
  • Implementation archive: 90 days idle.
  • Search includes archived tickets; Excel download; Days Remaining = business days.

Related: Process catalog · Ticket lifecycle

How it works — Calendar automation How it works

MS Calendar event name format:

Account Application_Deliverable_Frequency-Category[-Clearhealth]
Example: ACL COM_PA_Monthly-Regular
  • Non-daily: ticket created beginning of event day (EST); weekend → Monday unless Weekend Processing configured.
  • Daily: all next-month daily events created on last working day of current month (EST). New mid-month daily events → create manually.
  • Companions on create: PA → PAE / SCE / Cohort when same frequency exists; CM → HP when same frequency exists.
  • Author: OM User. Assignee/phase from DPCC → running ticket → Autopilot → product/frequency rules.
  • Email 9:15 AM NPT: Scheduled Production Processing (event vs ticket; red N/A rows). End of month: Missing Processing Events (excludes termed and zzz prefix).
How it works — Running ticket definition How it works
Ticket shape“Running” means open ticket in phase other than…
StandaloneClosed, Production Release
ChildClosed, Production Release, Scrub Release — OR prior parent not Closed/Production Release
ParentClosed, Production Release

If a non-daily create finds a running ticket → On Hold → Production CPM with hyperlink to the runner.

How it works — Manual create fields How it works
  • Account → Application → Product–Frequency (Deliverable-Frequency) → Category (Regular / Incremental / Bulk Incremental) → Type (I/M).
  • Maintenance: Scheduled Date (no past dates). Implementation: Processing For, Start/End Dates.
  • Special Processing requires valid numeric DPCC# (real Deermine) or create is blocked.
  • Incremental validation: Bulk Incremental must already exist for same Account/App/Product.
  • Versions: Incremental SE/Engine/Master Table inherit from last released Bulk Incremental.
  • Default SLA Status = On Track.
How it works — Archive timers How it works
  • Maintenance: auto-archive 150 days after Production Release, Scrub Release, Extract Release, or Closed (all frequencies including Quarterly).
  • Implementation: auto-archive after 90 days with no updates.
Checklist — 18.7 Production Manager behaviors Checklist
  • Scrub Resume appears under Assignments → Pending tab (OM-5419)
  • Create DPCC option available in Scrub Resume phase (OM-5505)
  • Auto-close behaviors for Account/Generic FM related tickets (OM-823)
  • File Unstaging phase fails when S3 unstage does not complete; verify History + Job Status
  • PAE Autopilot, Re-Unstage flag (M tickets), Scrub Only / CETL checkbox on eligible I tickets
  • Assignments tabs: Daily, Pending, Running, PAE, Recent; Sprint version display where enabled
  • Search API / Data Portal endpoints and Release Notification email rules for PA/PAE pairs
Summary and Key Takeaways
  • Calendar + Product–Frequency configuration determine 90% of ticket routing
  • Success factor: clear Pending queues daily; protect Incremental/Bulk rules
  • Next: master Phase Tracker Update and File Unstaging

Admin Default SLA → Accounts Client SLA Days
→ Ticket Release Date (Scheduled + Internal Refresh Days)
→ Dashboard Days Remaining + SLA Outside target

  2. Standup: Client SLA Outside target → Phase Tracker FRD/Release.

How it works — Client SLA Configuration How it works
  • SLA Reports → Configuration → Update SLA: enable Custom SLA per client; set product-wise Client SLA Days; reset to Default.
  • Adding a Production product in Accounts with Client SLA Days auto-checks that product in Update SLA.
  • Admin Deerwalk Default SLA seeds new products; Internal Refresh Days drive ticket Release Date (not the same field as Client SLA Days).
  • Client SLA Report month-wise distribution shows On Track vs Outside target; archived tickets handled per report filters.
Default SLA (Admin)
  → Client SLA Days (Accounts / Update SLA)
  → Ticket Scheduled + Internal Refresh Days = Release Date
  → Dashboard Days Remaining + Client SLA Outside target

How it works — EMR + Snowflake consolidation How it works

Client Processing grid merges EMR cluster status and Snowflake tracker status into one table (process/step, elapsed, status, cluster ids, processing phase).

  • EMR rows: clusterId, emrClusterId, stepName, stepStatus, processingPhase (e.g. ENGINE, SCRUB).
  • Snowflake rows: PROCEDURE_NAME, PROCESS_STATUS, STEP_ATTEMPT, PROCESSING_ELAPSED_TIME.
  • Filters: date range, Dailies vs Non-Dailies, client processing vs custom/IQR/splitter/parser/CA.
How it works — Control actions How it works
ActionEffect
Start ProcessingManually launch client processing or Daily IQR when cron missed
KillStop runaway cluster/step
ResumeContinue from failed/killed step
RebuildReconstruct cluster and rerun pipeline
ConfigurationHadoop/Snowflake client settings used by Autopilot Scrubbing / App Processing launch

Missing cluster settings in this Configuration is why Autopilot Scrubbing goes On Hold with “default cluster setting” errors.

How it works — Daily IQR pipeline How it works
  1. Files sync to deerwalk-iqr bucket.
  2. ~11:45 AM NPT scheduler runs Daily IQR cluster (thresholds from Admin).
  3. Outputs: Bad File Format, Bad Data, Drop/Spike, Record Count Variance, File Change.
  4. Over threshold → Jira File Issue; emails to Production/FME/Data SE as configured.
  5. If not executed → alert email; Processing starts manually from Dashboard.
Summary and Key Takeaways
  • Dashboard answers “is scrub healthy right now?”
  • Success factor: zero unexplained RUNNING > SLA threshold
  • Next: learn Kill/Resume playbooks with Processing mentor

Pseudonymization & Blinding Status

Pseudonymization de-identifies inbound files for Blinded Client applications before implementation/QC use. It is driven by the Application-level Blinded Client flag (Yes / File Set / No) and is monitored under Blinding Status. Regression suite 18.7.0 covers Accounts, Jobs, File Inventory, Daily IQR, Phase Tracker unstaging, and JetStore tracking tables.

Blinded Client flag Checklist
  • Location: Accounts → Application — default No
  • Editable by Admin and CPM only (Processing cannot edit)
  • Job-level “Blind run” flag is removed — blinding is application-driven
  • Persisted on om.clients.blinded_client
Trigger criteria (all required) Checklist
  1. Destination path matches File Inventory listing criteria (parameter count / path shape)
  2. File required / staging type is $ (Implementation / QC) — _! Production staging does not trigger
  3. Path second index contains onshore
  4. Destination client’s Application Blinded Client is Yes (or File Set as configured)
  5. Bucket is om-sqs or dasscrubinput (das-scrubinput)

Workflow

S3 Copy job completes → evaluate 5 criteria
  ├─ All match → JetStore pseudonymization (multi-output) → Blinding Status
  │                 → File Inventory ($ staged) → Move to Prod / Unstage
  └─ Any miss → no pseudonymization (may still inventory if path valid)
Operational behaviors Checklist
  • Multiple destinations: only paths meeting criteria blind; each valid path inserts into JetStore blind destination tables
  • Mixed $ and _! destinations: $ blinds; _! inventories as staged production without pseudonymization
  • Blinded Client is evaluated per client acronym in the destination path (e.g. ACL_AMG blinds, BAC_BAC may not)
  • After blinding: Move to Production and Unstage (FM UI or Phase Tracker File Unstaging) must still work
  • JetStore tracks progress in tables such as blind_file_destination_details, blind_file_test_progress, jetstore_blind_status, jetstore_generated_files
Roles and troubleshooting Checklist
IssueCheck
Expected blind did not runAll 5 criteria; Blinded Client flag; onshore index; $ staging; bucket name
File missing from inventoryPath parameter count / inventory listing rules
Cannot edit Blinded ClientUse Admin or CPM persona
Unstage after blindUse File Inventory or Phase Tracker File Unstaging

Related: Account Workflow · Jobs · File Inventory · JetStore · File Unstaging

Tip Pseudonymization requires ALL trigger criteria — partial matches must not blind files.

Ticket Processing Lifecycle

Ticket naming

  • Maintenance: Account_Application_Product_Month_Year_Frequency (e.g., ACL_COM_PA_10_18_M1)
  • Implementation: Account_Application_Product_I# (e.g., ACL_COM_PA_I1)

Creation methods

  1. Automated — MS Calendar events trigger maintenance tickets (daily: last working day of month for next month; other frequencies: day of event)
  2. Manual — Production Manager → Create Processing (CPM/Admin)

Auto-assignment logic

  • Open DPCC → On Hold, assigned to Production CPM
  • Running ticket exists (non-daily) → On Hold with link to running ticket
  • Autopilot = Yes → Waiting, Autopilot User
  • Autopilot = No, PA/CM/HP non-daily → File Arrangement, Processing Team
  • Autopilot = No, PA/CM/HP daily → Waiting, Daily Production

Archival

  • Maintenance: auto-archive 150 days after Production Release, Scrub Release, Extract Release, or Closed
  • Implementation: auto-archive after 90 days without updates
Deep Dive — Companion tickets & categories Deep Dive
  • Categories: Regular, Incremental, Bulk Incremental — Incremental needs Bulk Incremental.
  • Companions: PA→PAE/SCE; CM↔HP; flags reflect across linked tickets.
  • Parent/child: children scrub first; parent App Processing after all Scrub Release.
  • Last Release Ticket: Regular→Regular; Incremental→Bulk Incremental; manual override in Phase Tracker.

Frequently Used Scenarios

Create a manual maintenance ticket CPM / Admin
  1. Go to Production Manager → Processing Tickets → Create Processing.
  2. Select Account, Application, and Product-Frequency.
  3. Choose Type = Maintenance, Category (Regular/Incremental/Bulk Incremental).
  4. Set Scheduled Date (future date only).
  5. If Special Processing, check the flag and enter a valid DPCC number.
  6. Save — ticket auto-assigns to Production CPM by default.
Move files from QC to Production staging Processing / Admin
  1. Open File Manager → File Inventory → Staged Implementation Files.
  2. Filter to the client and job.
  3. Select file(s) and click Move to Production.
  4. Choose whether to keep or remove the development ($) copy.
  5. Verify files appear in Staged Production Files tab.
Unstage files for a processing ticket Processing / USDM
  1. Open the processing ticket in Phase Tracker.
  2. Set phase to File Unstaging, OR use Set Processing ID in File Inventory.
  3. Confirm — files move from _! path to active path and link to the ticket.
  4. Verify in File Inventory → Unstaged Files tab.
Release a maintenance processing run Processing / CPM
  1. Complete scrubbing and application processing phases.
  2. Update Phase Tracker to Production Release.
  3. Confirm assignee (varies by category/frequency — see Phase Tracker docs).
  4. Add mandatory Comment for Change if dates were modified.
  5. If re-releasing, respond to email confirmation prompts.
Investigate a missed file CPM / Processing
  1. Check File Inventory → Missed Production Files or Missed Files tab.
  2. Review Expected Date vs File Received Date.
  3. Check if file was received later (highlighted green when resolved).
  4. Review daily Missing File Report email (9:15 AM NPT).
  5. Create or verify File Issue Jira ticket if needed.

FAQ

What is a processing ticket?

A processing ticket tracks one client processing cycle — Implementation (I) or Maintenance (M) — for a specific Account, Application, and Product.

How are maintenance tickets created?

Most are auto-created from Microsoft Calendar events at 9:15 AM NPT. Daily tickets for the next month are created on the last working day of the current month.

What is File Received Date?

The date files were received for a maintenance ticket. Defaults to ticket creation; updates when leaving 'Waiting for Files' phase or manually by Admin/Processing.

What does Autopilot mean?

When enabled at Product-Frequency level, scheduled tickets auto-assign to Autopilot User in Waiting phase instead of manual file arrangement.

Why is my ticket On Hold?

Common reasons: open DPCC, another running ticket for same client-product-frequency, JetStore test failure, or extract upload failure.

What is the difference between Staged Implementation and Production files?

Implementation files ($ prefix) are for development/QC. Production files (_! prefix) are for live processing and can be unstaged to a processing ticket.

Who can set Production Release phase?

Restricted to Admin, Processing, and Production roles. CPM can edit dates and status but has limited phase access.

How do I find a ticket quickly?

Use Search on Dashboard or Production Manager → Assignments. Filter by Account, Application, Product, type, or date range.

Where do I monitor clusters and Daily IQR?

Processing Dashboard (EMR/Snowflake). Daily IQR ~11:45 AM NPT; Processing can Start Processing if automation failed.

How do Incremental tickets relate to Bulk Incremental?

Manual Incremental create requires an existing Bulk Incremental for the same Account, Application, and Product. Last Release Ticket for Incremental points at the latest Bulk Incremental release.

File-triggered vs phase-triggered jobs?

File-triggered: matching file arrives. Phase-triggered: Phase Tracker sets the job’s configured phase for that Account/Application.

How long before OM times out?

Idle session timeout is 45 minutes (single or multi-tab). After timeout or logout, you are redirected to login.

When does pseudonymization run?

Only when all criteria match: inventory-valid path, staging type $, onshore as second path index, Application Blinded Client enabled, and bucket om-sqs or dasscrubinput. See Pseudonymization.

Who can manage Vendor Schedule and FTP Actions?

DAC (ROLE_OM_VENDOR) plus Admin/privileged roles. See Vendor Module and FTP Accounts.

Where is Groupwise Billing documented?

Under OM Reports checklist enrichment and Custom Reports / billing report families (OM-4674).

Glossary of Terms

Account
Top-level client organization in OM (e.g., a health plan or employer group).
Application
A sub-entity under an Account — often maps to a product instance or branded environment.
Blinded Client
Application flag (Yes / File Set / No) that drives pseudonymization for qualifying inbound paths.
CPM
Client Production Manager — coordinates production processing schedules and releases.
DAC
Data Acquisition Coordinator (ROLE_OM_VENDOR) — vendor schedule, notifications, and FTP actions.
DPCC
Data Production Change Control — Jira ticket that may hold processing when open.
FM
File Manager — module for file inventory and vendor file operations.
FRD
File Received Date — when client files were received for a maintenance cycle.
IQR
Inbound Quality Review — daily automated file validation pipeline.
Maintenance (M)
Recurring production processing (monthly, weekly, daily, etc.).
Implementation (I)
One-time or project-based processing during client onboarding.
OIG
Office of Inspector General exclusion verification report (monthly custom job).
PA / PAE
Plan Analytics / Plan Analytics Extract — core analytics products.
Phase
Current step in a processing ticket lifecycle (e.g., Scrub Request, Production Release).
Pseudonymization
JetStore-backed de-identification when Blinded Client + path/staging criteria all match.
SQR
Scrub Quality Report — data quality metrics comparing processing runs.
Split File
S3 job type that publishes splitter work to DW-SPLIT-FILES.
USDM
US Data Manager — primary US-side data operations contact for an account.
Unstaging
Moving production files from staged (_!) to active processing paths linked to a ticket.
VCR
Vendor Change Request — automated Jira/Deermine vendor change workflow.
